statement: Without a causal mask and without positional information, f(x o pi) = f(x) o pi: the Transformer is permutation equivariant in its tokens.
source: pasted 1: 'a vanilla Transformer encoder is fundamentally permutation equivariant'

statement: With a causal mask and no positional information, token permutation equivariance fails.
source: pasted 1, applied to a decoder

statement: With rotary positional embeddings and no mask, token permutation equivariance fails.
source: pasted 1, applied to RoPE

statement: With a causal mask and rotary positional embeddings (a Llama-style decoder), token permutation equivariance fails.
source: pasted 1, applied to the models of this repository

statement: A causal decoder without positional information and with ONE layer: the logits at the last position are invariant under permutations of the earlier tokens.
source: derived: what survives of T2

statement: The same with TWO layers: the invariance of T5 fails (the second layer reads the first layer's prefix-dependent states).
source: derived: the depth at which T5 stops

statement: A signed permutation of the hidden coordinates, applied to every matrix that reads or writes the residual stream (embedding and head included) and to the norm weights, leaves f unchanged.
source: pasted 1 ('the exact same transformation to the weight matrices'), stated correctly

statement: H1 with the head tied to the embedding.
source: pasted 1, SmolLM2-style

statement: The rule as pasted, W_new = P W P^T, applied to the square weight matrices (here q and o) and nothing else, does not leave f unchanged.
source: pasted 1: 'W_new = P_C W P_C^T'

statement: A signed permutation of the hidden coordinates applied to the layers and the final norm but not to the embedding and the head ('encrypting the body') changes f.
source: pasted 1: 'applying a secret permutation matrix to an LLM's weights ... the model becomes entirely broken'

statement: Applying the permutation of H3 to the embedding and the head as well (the key) restores f exactly: f(body-only permuted, then keyed) = f.
source: pasted 1: 'an authorized user who possesses the permutation key ... perfectly decrypting'

statement: With the norm weights folded into the matrices that read them (the head made its own matrix), any orthogonal Q applied to the residual stream leaves f unchanged.
source: derived: 'computational invariance' (SliceGPT), pasted 4 (change of basis)

statement: In the unfolded parameterization (norm weights kept), with an untied head, an orthogonal Q applied to the stream with the readers conjugated, W -> W diag(gamma) Q diag(gamma)^-1, leaves f unchanged.
source: derived: the action of fold, rotate, unfold; found independently in the research notes

statement: The conjugated action of H4c on a model with a tied head and a learned final norm weight changes f.
source: derived: what the tie takes away from H4c

statement: Without the fold, a general orthogonal Q applied to the stream changes f.
source: derived: the necessity of the fold in H4

statement: With a tied head and a final norm weight that is not 1, an orthogonal Q applied to the stream (the tied head following) changes f: the final norm cannot be folded without untying.
source: derived: what the tie takes away from H4

statement: With a tied head and a final norm weight equal to 1 (and the layer norms folded), an orthogonal Q applied to the stream leaves f unchanged.
source: derived: H6 with the obstruction removed

statement: With LayerNorm (the mean subtracted), an orthogonal Q applied to the stream (norms folded) changes f unless Q fixes the all-ones vector.
source: derived: the stabilizer of the mean direction (SliceGPT converts LayerNorm to RMSNorm first)

statement: With LayerNorm, an orthogonal Q that fixes the all-ones vector (norms folded) leaves f unchanged.
source: derived: H7 restricted to the stabilizer of the all-ones vector

statement: Per key/value group, wv -> A wv and the group's o columns -> o A^-1, A in GL(hd), leaves f unchanged (the gauge of the value/output circuit).
source: derived: pasted 2 (W_OV); the product W_O W_V is gauge invariant

statement: The same A applied to wv alone changes f.
source: derived: the necessity of the compensation in A1

statement: With RoPE, per group and rotary plane, k -> M k and q -> M^-T q with M = [[a, -b], [b, a]] (a complex scalar) leaves f unchanged (the gauge of the query/key circuit).
source: derived: pasted 2 (W_QK); the commutant of the rotations

statement: With RoPE, k -> A k and q -> A^-T q with A a general element of GL(hd) changes f.
source: derived: pasted 2 ('W_Q W_K as a static operator') fails under RoPE

statement: Without positional information, k -> A k and q -> A^-T q with A in GL(hd) leaves f unchanged.
source: derived: A4 without RoPE

statement: A permutation of the key/value groups and of the query heads inside each group (with the matching permutation of the o columns) leaves f unchanged.
source: derived

statement: A permutation of the query heads (and the o columns) that moves a head to another key/value group, the key and value matrices staying, changes f.
source: derived: the group structure of A6 is necessary

statement: A permutation of the hidden units of the gated block, and a nonzero scale c on each up row with 1/c on the matching down column, leaves f unchanged.
source: derived

statement: A scale on the gate rows (with the down columns compensating) changes f: the gate nonlinearity is not homogeneous.
source: derived: the limit of M1

statement: A scale c_i on a norm weight and 1/c_i on column i of every matrix that reads it leaves f unchanged (the fold of H4 is the case c = 1/gamma).
source: derived

statement: Folding every norm weight into the matrices that read it (RMSNorm or LayerNorm) leaves f unchanged.
source: derived

statement: The composition of the symmetries H1, A1, A3, A6, M1 and N1, with random elements, leaves f unchanged.
source: derived: the group generated by the exact symmetries

statement: With RMSNorm, subtracting from every embedding row its mean (what the fuse_layer_norms of QuaRot and SpinQuant do for every model type), the head kept, changes f.
source: derived: a published code practice; the all-ones component of the stream is part of the RMS

statement: With LayerNorm (the mean subtracted), subtracting from every embedding row its mean leaves f unchanged.
source: derived: the case in which the centering of H8 is exact

statement: The KV cache is unchanged by a signed permutation of the hidden coordinates (H1).
source: derived: the cache is a function of the normalized input and the input projections

statement: K1 with the head tied to the embedding.
source: derived

statement: The KV cache is unchanged by an orthogonal Q applied to the stream with the norm weights folded (H4).
source: derived: computational invariance does not touch the cache

statement: The KV cache is unchanged by the gauge of the feed-forward units (M1).
source: derived

statement: The KV cache is unchanged by the gauge of the norm weights (N1).
source: derived

statement: A permutation of the key/value groups (A6) permutes the groups of the KV cache: the new group g holds the old group gp[g].
source: derived

statement: The KV cache is not unchanged by a non-trivial permutation of the key/value groups.
source: derived: the necessity of the permutation in K4

statement: Under the value/output gauge (A1) the keys are unchanged and the values of group g are mapped by A_g: v -> A_g v.
source: derived

statement: The KV cache is not unchanged by the value/output gauge: the values move.
source: derived: what the gauge freedom costs a cache

statement: Under the query/key gauge of RoPE (A3) the values are unchanged and each key plane of the cache is mapped by its complex scalar: (x1, x2) -> (a x1 - b x2, b x1 + a x2).
source: derived: a complex scalar commutes with the rotation by position, so the stored (rotated) key is mapped by the same scalar

statement: The KV cache is not unchanged by the query/key gauge of RoPE: the keys move.
source: derived

statement: The cache of the model with the permuted body and the unpermuted embedding ('encrypting the body', H3) is not the original's: the body reads coordinates that the embedding does not write.
source: pasted 1, applied to the cache

statement: The cache of the model with the permuted body and the key applied at the interface (H3k) is the original's: the cache is in the public gauge, so a permutation of the hidden dimension hides nothing in it.
source: pasted 1 ('perfectly decrypting'), applied to the cache; the weights are permuted, what the model computes with is not
